STAMP REFRESHED, NUMBER UNCHANGED. The old stamp named a commit the 2026-09-02 sync replayed away, so `--list` flagged it ORPHANED-BASE and architecture.yml exited 2 asking to be re-measured rather than comparing anything -- neither green nor red. Re-measured in a clean detached worktree of 1ad4d29c24e and it reads exactly what the floor already said, so only the stamp moves.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

STAMPED, NOT MOVED. The floor carried no `measured_at` at all, so it was a number nobody could reproduce: the guard that refuses a stamp this branch never had cannot fire on a floor with no stamp, and an unstamped floor may never have been true of any tree. Re-measured on a clean detached worktree at the stamped commit -- python tooling/architecture/py_shadowed_member.py --addon addons --count -- and it reads 0, equal to the floor. The count does not move; only the stamp does.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

stock/product_template.py: 6 -> 0, and the whole of the -6 is one duplicated block leaving the file.

ProductTemplate defined _search_variant_quantity twice, sixty lines apart, and
Python keeps the last. The survivor called Product._get_domain_locations()
(removed -- the scope moved to stock.location) and passed five positional
arguments to _prepare_quantities_vals, which takes two. So every search on
product.template.qty_available / qty_available_virtual / qty_incoming /
qty_outgoing raised AttributeError before reaching the database, while the same
search on product.product -- never shadowed -- worked.

The fix was the other definition. Deleted with it: _filter_quantity_in_python,
which only the dead block called and which is line-for-line the module-level
filter_quantity_in_python that the file already imports; the four one-line
_search_qty_* delegators, duplicated verbatim; and _resolve_diagram_products,
byte-identical to its twin.

Eight tests across four files were already failing on this at HEAD. Measured in
a detached worktree, -i stock --test-tags /stock, failure sets diffed by name:
16 -> 8, the eight template-search ones green and nothing newly broken. What
remains is unrelated (TestPendingQuantAvailability x7 calls a method that exists
nowhere but in its own tests; TestOrderpointAudit x1 is an assertion mismatch).

Both governed scopes are now zero, so this gate is a contract rather than a floor.
